newsitem.title: INDIA: India call money ends marginally up on late demand.
newsitem.headline: India call money ends marginally up on late demand.

text.p: Indian call money firmed up on late demand to end Wednesday at 3.0-3.5 percent, up from opening quotes of 2.25-3.0 percent, dealers said.
They said most of the day's trade was done between 2.0 percent and 2.5 percent.
"Rates went up towards close of trade on some late demand from a few banks," said a dealer at a foreign bank. "But this was in thin trade and most of the deals were at lower levels."
Dealers said they expected call money rates to open around three percent on Thursday.
Prices of government securities were mixed in moderate trade, dealers said.
They said banks were reluctant to take trading positions ahead of the financial year-end on March 31.
"Further there is also some uncertainty among market participants over liquidity after advance tax payments," said a dealer at a state-run bank.
Companies are required to pay their last instalment of advance taxes for the current financial year by March 15. Analysts' estimates of the payments range between 30 billion and 50 billion rupees.
Dealers said the 13.40 percent government of India 1999 traded on Wednesday at 102.01 rupees against its last traded price of 102.01 and the 13.50 percent 1998 at 103.14 rupees against 103.06.
Treasury bills maturing in April yielded 7.5 percent, May bill 8.15 percent and bills maturing in February 1998 at 10.3 percent, dealers said.
A certificate of deposit (CD) maturing in end-March was traded at a yield of 7.5 percent and an April-maturity CD at 8.0 percent, they said.
